text:
maria: kicking off cuda-12 image rollout to eu-west and asia-southeast1 pools now. small canary on 3 nodes first, full batch in 30m. please watch for pod restarts. :eyes:
jon: seeing a couple of pods OOM and some failed container starts in asia-southeast1. logs show PTX JIT errors and ld-linux complaints. rolling hold?
sanjay: hold the rollout. cordoning the remaining canary nodes in that region. i'll drain the ones flapping.
maria: ack hold. cordon done for asia-southeast1-canary-{1..2}.
jon: paste of one error from kubelet logs:
```
E c10: cuda call failed: PTX-JIT compilation error: 'ptx not supported for sm_70'
Container runtime failed to start: /lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
modprobe: ERROR: could not insert 'nvidia_uvm': Unknown symbol in module
```
ashley: this looks like a mismatch: the container image was rebuilt with nvcc that emitted PTX targeting sm_80+ by default. older node drivers in asia still on 525.x can't JIT newer PTX. also some of our base images replaced glibc (hence ld-linux mismatch) when we switched the build base to debian-bookworm.
maria: oh yikes — so two simultaneous mismatches from our container rebuilds (toolkit + base image).
infra-bot: [alert] asia-southeast1: 6 nodes in flapping state, 18 pods affected, autoscaler launched 4 extra nodes. Estimated spend delta: ~$220 last 2h.
sanjay: autoscaler params need a quick tweak to prevent cascade during this kind of failure. lowering scale-up aggressiveness for asia-southeast1 for now.
jon: workaround ideas: 1) revert to pre-rebuild image tag (cuda11-compat:v3) 2) or set NVCC flags and rebuild images with PTX for sm_70 compatibility and keep libc consistent 3) roll driver forward on nodes in region (risky mid-day)
ashley: i'm rebuilding a minimal patch image with: `nvcc --generate-code=arch=compute_70,code=sm_70 --keep-ptx` and using debian-bullseye base + explicit ldd checks. will push a canary tag in ~15m.
maria: good. also please add a quick entry to the release notes about "do not switch base distro in same rollout" so we avoid glibc/ld path drift.
sanjay: current plan: revert canaries to previous image and suspend rollout; cordon remaining nodes until rebuild verified. we'll keep autoscaler conservative and manually scale if needed.
jon: i've rolled back 4 canary pods to `cuda11-compat:v3` manually on the flapping nodes — they stabilized. leaving one canary as-is for ashley's test.
ashley: pushed `cuda12-ptx-sm70-patch:canary`. sample pod starts clean on a repro node with driver 525.85. runbook step: add env `CUDA_FORCE_PTXJIT=1` is a no-op for this mismatch, so don't rely on it.
maria: thanks. action items: ashley finish rebuild and validation (P0), jon update autoscaler doc + revert policy (P1), sanjay coordinate node driver upgrade window for next maintenance (P2).
infra-bot: [note] incident created: INC-2026-0483 (cuda12-image-rebuild-fallout). assigned to eng-infra.
jon: quick FYI — we also hit a kernel module symbol mismatch on two nodes: `nvidia_uvm` failed due to kernel headers mismatch after a security patch last week. some nodes require reboot to match running kernel vs installed modules. scheduling reboots in the maintenance window.
sanjay: reboots scheduled. will target non-prod pools first then prod after manual validation.
maria: thanks team — holding the global rollout until we verify rebuilt images and a node upgrade plan. postmortem draft will include build matrix (nvcc/toolkit/base distro) and a preflight check: run `ldd /lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2` and `cuobjdump --list-ptx` on images before rolling.
ashley: adding a CI job to detect PTX architecture >= max driver supported and a lint that flags base distro changes in the same release.
maria: huge help. closing hold once ashley's canary is green for 1h. :thumbsup:
